title: Gates calls for taxing AI, reserving jobs for humans
source_used: ETHRWorld (opening paragraph only); Telangana Today and FourWeekMBA accounts of the same CNN interview
key_facts: On CNN's State of the Union on Sunday 11 Oct 2026, Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates said society will have to decide, in the years ahead, how to tax AI or robot usage and where to preserve human jobs.
Host Jake Tapper asked about Gates's earlier warning that AI job losses across virtually all sectors would be 'unprecedented' and his call to reserve some education and health-care jobs for humans.
Gates said reserving work for humans 'may sound bizarre' now, but 'we will get there'.
He said AI 'changes the world more than all previous technologies' and that he is watching how fast models improve and the incentive to use AI in place of human labour.
He named bad actors using AI, especially in cyberattacks, as the most immediate danger and said loss of control is 'years away' (FourWeekMBA, reading CNN's rush transcript).
He expects that 'over the next year, we will move beyond self-governance' by AI companies, with government safety bodies like those for aviation and medicines (Telangana Today).
Gates said he has heard from 'a number of politicians' and hopes 'in time' to talk with President Trump and his key people.
None of the accounts read gives a tax rate, design or date; the remarks are expectations and opinion, not a policy proposal.
quote_evidence: In the years ahead, we really do need to make a decision as a society, how do we tax AI usage or robot usage?
the idea that you need to reserve things for humans may sound bizarre, but, in fact, we will get there
Gates was asked by host Jake Tapper about his earlier warning that the breadth of AI job losses across virtually all sectors would be "unprecedented"
why_it_matters_hint: A prominent AI-era figure puts taxing AI and keeping some jobs human-only on the public agenda, though only as a question for society.
event_date: 11 Oct 2026 (CNN State of the Union interview)
notes: ETHRWorld page returned only its opening paragraph (719 chars). The rest comes from Telangana Today (https://telanganatoday.com/bill-gates-says-society-must-decide-how-to-tax-ai-and-protect-human-jobs) and FourWeekMBA (https://fourweekmba.com/ai-gates-says-ai-cyberattacks-will-bring-negative-surprises/), which says it read CNN's rush transcript; CNN's own page was not opened. Gates's separate Reuters interview was carried in our 9 Oct 2026 edition; these CNN remarks are new.
